question.prompt: The point \((-1, -2)\) is rotated \(270^\circ\) counterclockwise about the point \((3, 1).\) What are the coordinates of its new position?

solutions.title: Turn the horizontal and vertical legs
solutions.explanation:
A \(270^\circ\) counterclockwise rotation is a \(90^\circ\) clockwise rotation, so horizontal and vertical directions simply turn a quarter-turn.

Call the center \(C=(3,1)\) and the original point \(P=(-1,-2)\). Introduce \(T=(-1,1)\). Going from \(C\) to \(T\) means moving \(4\) units left; going from \(T\) to \(P\) means moving \(3\) units down.

Under the clockwise quarter-turn, left becomes up and down becomes left, while lengths stay the same. Thus \(T\) moves to
\[
T'=(3,1+4)=(3,5).
\]
The image of \(P\) lies \(3\) units left of \(T'\), so its coordinates are
\[
(3-3,5)=\boxed{(0,5)}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\textbf{B}\).

solutions.title: Rotate using complex numbers
solutions.explanation:
Complex numbers turn the rotation into multiplication by \(-i\).

Represent \((a,b)\) by \(a+bi\), where \(i^2=-1\). Multiplication by \(-i\) sends the rightward direction \(1\) to the downward direction \(-i\), and the upward direction \(i\) to the rightward direction \(1\). By distributing over the horizontal and vertical components, this performs a \(90^\circ\) clockwise rotation, equivalent to the requested \(270^\circ\) counterclockwise rotation.

The center is represented by \(c=3+i\), and the original point by \(p=-1-2i\). Subtracting \(c\) gives the displacement from the center:
\[
p-c=-4-3i.
\]
Rotate this displacement and then add the center back:
\[
\begin{aligned}
c+(-i)(p-c)
&=3+i+(-i)(-4-3i)\\
&=3+i+4i-3\\
&=5i.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore the new position is \(\boxed{(0,5)}\), choice \(\textbf{B}\).
